full_text_en:
Jiangsu Provincial Materials Group Light Industry and Textile Corporation v. (Hong Kong) Top Capital Holdings Ltd. and (Canada) Prince Development Ltd. — appeal of dispute over tort damages

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): (Hong Kong) Top Capital Holdings Ltd. (TOPCAPITALHOLDINGSLTD).

Legal Representative: Grant Xue (GRANTXUE), General Manager of the Company.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): (Canada) Prince Development Ltd. (PRINCEDEVELOPMENTLTD).

Legal Representative: Grant Xue (GRABTXUE), General Manager of the Company.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Jiangsu Provincial Materials Group Light Industry and Textile Corporation.

Legal Representative: Cheng Haiyan, General Manager of the Company.

Appellants (Hong Kong) Top Capital Holdings Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Top Capital") and (Canada) Prince Development Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Prince Development"), dissatisfied with the civil ruling of first instance by the Jiangsu Higher People's Court in the case of dispute over tort damages with the Appellee Jiangsu Provincial Materials Group Light Industry and Textile Corporation (hereinafter referred to as "Light Industry and Textile Corporation"), appealed to the Supreme People's Court.

The court of first instance, the Jiangsu Higher People's Court, found the following facts upon trial: On May 5, 1996, the Plaintiff Light Industry and Textile Corporation and the Defendant Top Capital entered into Sales Contract No. CC960505, stipulating that Top Capital would sell 5,000 metric tons of used ordinary electric motors to Light Industry and Textile Corporation at USD 348.9 per metric ton. On May 6 of the same year, Light Industry and Textile Corporation and the Defendant Prince Development entered into Sales Contract No. CC960506, stipulating that Prince Development would sell 5,000 metric tons of used ordinary electric motors to Light Industry and Textile Corporation at USD 348.9 per metric ton. Article 8 of both contracts expressly provided: "Any dispute arising from the execution of this contract or in connection with this contract shall be settled by friendly negotiation between the parties; if negotiation fails, the dispute shall be submitted to the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission for arbitration in accordance with its arbitration rules. The arbitral award is final and binding upon both parties." After the goods arrived at the port, inspection by the commodity inspection authority revealed: The total weight of the goods was 9,586.323 metric tons, and "this shipment mainly consists of various types of scrap structural parts, scrap steel pipes, scrap gearboxes, scrap round steel, etc." Light Industry and Textile Corporation then filed a lawsuit on the grounds that Top Capital and Prince Development had committed torts causing it losses. Within the response period, Top Capital and Prince Development raised objections to jurisdiction, stating that the parties had voluntarily reached an arbitration agreement for contract disputes, and the people's court should not accept the case according to law.

The Jiangsu Higher People's Court held that: This case is a dispute over tort damages arising from fraud. Although the sales contracts between the Plaintiff Light Industry and Textile Corporation and the Defendants Top Capital and Prince Development contain an arbitration clause, the Defendants, by utilizing the contracts to commit fraud, have exceeded the scope of contract performance and constituted a tort. The dispute between the parties is no longer a dispute over contractual rights and obligations, but a dispute over tort damages. Light Industry and Textile Corporation has the right to file a tort action in court and is not bound by the arbitration clause agreed upon by the parties. The objections to jurisdiction raised by Top Capital and Prince Development are unfounded. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 243 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the court ruled on September 10, 1997: the objections to jurisdiction raised by Top Capital and Prince Development are dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, the Defendants Top Capital and Prince Development, being dissatisfied, appealed to the Supreme People's Court. Top Capital and Prince Development alleged: (1) The cause of action in Light Industry and Textile Corporation's complaint is not supported by facts; it deliberately confuses tort liability and contractual liability, attempting to circumvent legal provisions and contractual agreements. Based on the content of the case, the cause of action should be contract dispute. The parties have voluntarily reached an arbitration agreement for contract disputes, and according to law, the court of first instance should not have accepted this case. (2) During the procedural hearing, the court of first instance, without substantive trial, made a determination on Light Industry and Textile Corporation's allegation that Top Capital and Prince Development committed "fraud", which is an unlawful ruling. Therefore, they request the reversal of the first-instance ruling and a ruling that the people's court shall not accept this case.

The Plaintiff Light Industry and Textile Corporation argued in defense: According to the provisions of the Arbitration Law and relevant arbitration practices, the arbitral tribunal only hears disputes between the parties who have concluded the arbitration agreement; it has no jurisdiction over third parties who have an interest in the legal facts arising between the parties, cannot conduct a hearing, and its award cannot involve third parties. Based on the facts of this case, this is not a mere contract dispute; it involves issues of tortious fraud and smuggling crimes. The relevant acts and results also directly involve third parties. If this case were heard through arbitration proceedings, it would clearly be detrimental to ascertaining the facts of the case and to protecting the legitimate rights and interests of the parties. If the people's court hears this case, it can, by virtue of the judicial power conferred by law, thoroughly ascertain the facts, hold the wrongdoers accountable, and protect the legitimate rights and interests of the parties. Therefore, they request that the first-instance ruling be upheld and the appeal of the Defendants Top Capital and Prince Development be dismissed.

The Supreme People's Court held that: The focus of the dispute in this case is whether the arbitral institution has the authority to make an award on the tort dispute between the parties. The Arbitration Law of the PRC came into effect on October 1, 1995. Article 2 of that Law states: "Disputes over contracts and other disputes over property rights and interests arising between citizens, legal persons, and other organizations with equal status may be submitted to arbitration." Article 3 states: "The following disputes may not be submitted to arbitration: (1) disputes over marriage, adoption, guardianship, maintenance, and inheritance; (2) administrative disputes that shall be handled by administrative authorities according to law." Article 2 of the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission Arbitration Rules (hereinafter referred to as the "Arbitration Rules") also expressly provides that the Commission "...resolves disputes arising from international or foreign-related contractual or non-contractual economic and trade matters..." From the facts and reasons stated in the Appellee Light Industry and Textile Corporation's complaint in the court of first instance, the alleged tortious acts of the Appellants Top Capital and Prince Development all arose during the signing and performance of Sales Contracts No. CC960505 and No. CC960506, and also occurred after the implementation of the Arbitration Law. Article 8 of both contracts expressly provides: "Any dispute arising from the execution of this contract or in connection with this contract shall be settled by friendly negotiation between the parties; if negotiation fails, the dispute shall be submitted to the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission for arbitration in accordance with its arbitration rules. The arbitral award is final and binding upon both parties." According to the above provisions of the Arbitration Law and the Arbitration Rules, the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission has the authority to accept tort disputes, and therefore this case should be resolved through arbitration, and the people's court has no jurisdiction. The court of first instance's opinion that Light Industry and Textile Corporation's filing of a tort action is not bound by the arbitration clause agreed upon by the parties is clearly contrary to the Arbitration Law and the Arbitration Rules; moreover, when Light Industry and Textile Corporation filed the lawsuit alleging that Top Capital and Prince Development used the contracts to commit fraud, the court of first instance, without substantive trial, confirmed this by a substantive judgment and, by way of a ruling, determined that the two appellants used the contracts to commit fraud, which violates the provisions of Article 140 of the Civil Procedure Law of our country concerning the scope of application of rulings, and is also procedurally erroneous. The appellants' grounds for appeal are established and should be supported. In this case, the parties explicitly agreed in the contracts to resolve disputes through arbitration; so long as the contracts have not been confirmed as invalid by the relevant authorities, the parties shall be bound by the terms of the contracts. Even if this case involves third parties, in the event that the arbitral tribunal cannot pursue the liability of third parties, Light Industry and Textile Corporation may file a separate lawsuit in the people's court against the third parties as defendants, and the legitimate rights and interests of the parties can still be protected. The defense of Light Industry and Textile Corporation that "this case involves third parties...only by having the people's court hear this case can the facts be ascertained and the legitimate rights and interests of the parties be protected" is not adopted.

In conclusion, all parties in this case shall be bound by the arbitration clause stipulated in the contracts, and the disputes arising shall be resolved through arbitration; the people's court has no jurisdiction. The ruling made by the Jiangsu Higher People's Court erred in the application of law and shall be reversed. Accordingly, the Supreme People's Court, pursuant to Article 111(2) and Article 257, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, ruled on May 31, 1998: 1. The civil ruling (1996) Su Jing Chu Zi No. 78-1 of the Jiangsu Higher People's Court is reversed; 2. The lawsuit filed by Jiangsu Provincial Materials Group Light Industry and Textile Corporation is dismissed.
